title: The tool surface follows the claim

record.surface: back in the conversation, with the requirements panel, the status strip and the WebMCP tools panel all visible on the page. Open the tools panel by hand if the window is short enough that it stayed folded
prompts: I have just corrected the drivable answer on the page myself. Read the claim again and tell me what changed and what it needs now.
must_show: a read_claim_state or get_requirements entry appearing in the tool call ledger, so the read back the narration describes is on screen and is not taken on trust
the requirements list changing, with the reason printed beside each entry
the status strip reading 9 tools registered
the get_assistance_options row in the WebMCP tools panel, reading Registered because the claim says the vehicle cannot be driven, and the agent naming the tool in its answer
the roadside collection entry in the requirements list, with the words saying no tool on this page reaches it and a person has to act on it
record.note: The count is asked for here as a STATE, 9, and not as a change from 8. The change happens in 04-human-corrects: startToolSurface in src/webmcp/register.js is subscribed to the store, so correcting the drivable answer is what publishes get_assistance_options, and a take that starts afterwards cannot contain that transition. It is not instant, and an earlier version of this note said it was: src/webmcp/register.js:542 says "Reconciles are queued behind one another because registering is asynchronous and the store is not", so the strip can take a moment. That does not change what this take shows, which is the count as a state. The narration says the correction has already published the tool, which is what this take can actually show. What is new here is the agent reading the claim again, finding the tool, and reading out a requirement that no tool on the page can close. The reason a tool was published is readable only on the tool row itself. The page also announces it, but that announcement goes to the live region, which the stylesheet clips to one pixel for screen readers, so it is never on camera and is not asked for here.
